author: Codex paired expert author A

source_artifacts.claim: Current campaign order puts level_02 at position 1 and level_01 at position 2.
Current definition of level_01: a powered moving lift, occupancy-based DNA_OPEN door pad, two-weight RESTORE latch on the lift, no authored hazards, collectibles, and two exits.
Current scene assigns Gem's wall scheme to DNA_OPEN/RESTORE and Cana's lift drain to RESTORE.
Pad weight and occupancy determine activation; a latch stays active, and pad effects open doors or power platforms.
A requiresPower platform has no power until enabled; motion follows a periodic offset.
A moving platform advances only when active, motored, and powered, and carries its riders.
Gem's bubble applies short role-specific effects; the restore pad can counter the authored bubble attack.

prior_knowledge.concept: A role-specific hold pad can open a barrier; pad effects are a way to alter routes.

evidence.claim: level_02 precedes this room in campaign order.
Earlier level_02 introduces Isp HOLD and Pac RESCUE as door-changing pads.

prior_knowledge.concept: Bubble effects differ by hero; an earlier onboarding text says bubbles float Isp and Pac can bounce from the gold top or become stuck at the side.

evidence.claim: Earlier position-1 visible onboarding text introduces the different bubble interactions.

prior_knowledge.concept: Both matching exits are required to finish a room.

evidence.claim: The first campaign room visibly introduces the both-exits objective.

prior_knowledge.concept: A restore pad attached to a moving lift powers it only after two units of weight occupy it together; no authored crates are present, so both heroes supply the threshold.

evidence.claim: The lift requires power and the attached RESTORE pad accepts any weight with minWeight 2; level_01 has no crates.
Current-source replay records both heroes occupying the RESTORE pad at weight 2, latched and active.

mechanics.fact: Isp's DNA_OPEN hold pad opens the Pac-only DNA wall while occupied. The wall can close again after Isp leaves unless another active pad effect opens it.

evidence.claim: DNA_OPEN accepts Isp, requires hold activation, opens dna_wall, and dna_wall blocks Pac.
Unlatched pads are active only at their occupancy threshold; barriers reset closed before active pad effects reopen them.

mechanics.fact: The glucose lift starts unpowered. Its RESTORE pad is attached to the lift, accepts either hero, and requires total weight 2; with no crates, both heroes must occupy it simultaneously. The latch then powers the moving lift and also opens DNA wall.

evidence.claim: The lift requires power; RESTORE attaches to it, accepts any actor, requires weight 2, latches, and powers the lift while opening dna_wall.
Each eligible hero contributes one weight, the minWeight threshold controls activation, and latch activation persists.
RequiresPower disables default power and the authored lift offset follows a periodic motion.
Powered moving platforms move and carry their riders.

mechanics.fact: Gem's bubble targets the start-area pad, and RESTORE counters the attack; a hit gives Isp FLOAT or Pac STICKY for a short duration.

evidence.claim: The room authors Gem's bubble attack and names RESTORE as its interruption pad.
Bubble effect depends on hero: FLOAT for Isp and STICKY for Pac, with a short duration.

mechanics.fact: There are four hero-owned collectibles in addition to the matching exits; the mandatory goal remains both exits.

evidence.claim: The definition lists four collectibles separately from the two matching exit records.

legal_routes.name: Open DNA wall, co-occupy RESTORE, ride lift, and finish both exits (one current-source native replay)

steps.goal: Open the Pac-only DNA wall so Pac can pass to the lift area.
steps.action: Move Isp onto DNA_OPEN and keep the pad occupied while Pac moves right through the open wall.
steps.expected_feedback: The held pad opens the wall while Isp remains on it.
steps.observed_feedback: The current-source replay records Isp on DNA_OPEN and dna_wall open at frame 80; at frame 640 Pac is beyond the wall while Isp still occupies the pad.

evidence.claim: Isp's occupancy-based pad opens the wall that blocks Pac.
At frame 80 Isp occupies DNA_OPEN and the DNA wall is open.
At frame 640 Pac is across the wall while Isp is still holding DNA_OPEN.

steps.goal: Restart and power the lift by reaching the two-weight RESTORE pad together.
steps.action: After the wall crossing, move both heroes to the lift's attached RESTORE pad and occupy it at the same time; an earlier solo occupancy is insufficient.
steps.expected_feedback: One hero contributes weight 1 and leaves the pad inactive; both heroes contribute weight 2, latch RESTORE, power the lift, and reopen the wall.
steps.observed_feedback: At frame 1470 Isp is the only occupant and RESTORE is inactive at weight 1. At frame 1646 both heroes are on the pad, weight is 2, RESTORE is latched, and the DNA wall is open.

evidence.claim: The lift requires power and its attached RESTORE pad requires weight 2 before powering it and opening the wall.
At frame 1470 only Isp occupies RESTORE; weight 1 is below the threshold and the pad remains inactive.
At frame 1646 both heroes occupy RESTORE at weight 2; it is active and latched.

steps.goal: Ride the powered lift to the exit balcony and reach both matching exits.
steps.action: Stay aboard as the lift rises, then jump to the balcony and move each hero to its matching exit.
steps.expected_feedback: The moving platform carries riders upward; the balcony provides the final path to both exits.
steps.observed_feedback: At frame 1886 both heroes are supported by the rising lift. The replay then records both jumping toward the balcony and completes at frame 2393 with both heroes at matching exits and zero deaths.

evidence.claim: A powered moving platform carries its riders.
At frame 1886 both heroes ride the lift as it moves upward.
At frame 2153 both heroes are on the exit balcony after the jump from the lift.
At frame 2393 the replay is complete with both matching exits reached and no deaths.
Accepted ordinary-input interval schedule for level_01.
The retained schedule replays against current source to both exits with no death.

isp: Holds DNA_OPEN so Pac can cross the first wall.
Moves to the lift and occupies RESTORE with Pac; Isp alone leaves its two-weight threshold unmet.
Rides the powered lift, jumps to the exit balcony, and enters the Isp exit.
pac: Crosses the DNA wall while Isp holds its pad.
Joins Isp on RESTORE to reach weight 2 and latch lift power.
Rides the lift, jumps to the balcony, and enters the Pac exit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Only one hero reaches the RESTORE pad, or the pair do not overlap there at the same time.
common_mistakes.consequence: The pad stays below weight 2, so it does not latch and the lift remains unpowered.
common_mistakes.recovery: Bring the second hero onto the attached pad while the first remains on it. If the pair miss a ride after powering the lift, the visible cue says to wait at the side; the lift follows a repeating vertical motion so they can reboard on its return. No failed attempt or recovery was exercised in the replay.

evidence.claim: RESTORE needs weight 2 and the lift requires power.
Solo occupancy leaves RESTORE inactive at weight 1.
Visible cue says 'Missed it? Wait at the side.'
The lift's vertical motion repeats on an authored period.

common_mistakes.mistake: Isp steps off DNA_OPEN before Pac has cleared the wall.
common_mistakes.consequence: The hold pad becomes inactive and the Pac-only wall closes, blocking Pac from continuing through it.
common_mistakes.recovery: Pac can turn back to the safe starting floor while Isp reoccupies DNA_OPEN, then cross again. This is a source-and-layout inference, not a failed sequence demonstrated by the route replay.

evidence.claim: The floor is continuous and the hold pad is near the start; it controls the Pac-only wall.
Leaving an unlatched pad removes its active door effect.

optional_collectibles: The definition lists four hero-owned collectibles separately from both exits. They are outside the mandatory route score. The retained replay result does not preserve pickup totals, so it does not establish which items, if any, this schedule collected.

reasoning.rationale: The route depends first on an Isp-held door, then on recognizing that two heroes must occupy RESTORE together to power the lift and reopen the wall, followed by riding it to the balcony. The trace confirms the weight threshold and order. First-pass reasoning 2 identified a two-cell lift dependency but could not see that the two characters themselves supply the weight.

evidence.claim: The route combines the DNA_OPEN door with the two-weight restore/power pad.
The native route records the simultaneous weight-2 activation.

cooperation.rationale: The route contains a handoff from Isp holding the first door to Pac crossing it, then requires both players to occupy the moving lift's RESTORE pad simultaneously. This mutual dependency is confirmed by the source threshold and the replay's solo weight-1 versus joint weight-2 snapshots. First-pass cooperation was unknown because the idle frames could not reveal the pad requirement.

evidence.claim: Isp's door hold is followed by a two-weight pad that either hero may occupy.
Both heroes are simultaneously on the pad at the threshold that latches it.

execution.rationale: The route calls for several controlled movements: crossing the first wall, jumping from the left onto the lift, synchronizing occupancy on its small attached pad, riding the lift, then jumping to the elevated balcony. The sampled schedule completes without death, but the repeated jumps and shared placement make execution more than simple walking. First-pass execution was unknown because no movement was observed.

evidence.claim: The route includes an unpowered moving lift and elevated exit balcony.
The accepted schedule contains staged movement and jump intervals for the lift and balcony route.
The current-source replay completes both exits without death.

timing.rationale: The lift moves on a repeating eight-second cycle and its boarding side is authored as left; the screen cue says to jump from the left and to wait at the side if missed. The safe wait-and-return option makes the window readable and repeatable rather than narrow. First-pass timing was unknown because idle views did not establish the lift cycle.

evidence.claim: The lift has an eight-second periodic vertical motion, boards from the left, and requires power.
Visible cue directs a left-side jump and tells the player to wait at the side if the lift is missed.
The replay shows the powered lift carrying both heroes upward.

hazards.rationale: The source defines no authored hazards and a continuous floor beneath the route; missing the powered lift can return a player to that floor. The native replay completes without death. Gem's bubble can cause a temporary status effect, but the trace does not show dangerous exposure, and the effect is not counted as a hazard by itself. First-pass hazards were unknown because screenshots showed no contact consequence.

evidence.claim: A continuous floor supports the room below the lift and exit balcony.
The only barrier is a door and the hazards array is empty.
The sampled current-source schedule reaches both exits without death.

novelty.rationale: The preceding level_02 introduces Isp holding a door and Pac using a rescue latch, but this room changes the dependency: both characters must supply weight together on a pad attached to an unpowered moving lift. This new simultaneous power-and-ride model goes beyond transferring the earlier door-pad behavior. First-pass novelty 2 saw a new lift condition but not that both heroes themselves supply the threshold.

evidence.claim: level_02 is the immediately preceding campaign position.
The new room introduces a requires-power moving platform and a two-weight attached latch.
The replay confirms both heroes jointly activate the new lift mechanic.

recovery_cost.rationale: The screen explicitly says to wait at the side if the lift is missed, and the source shows a repeating lift cycle over a continuous floor. This suggests a safe retry with a short wait rather than repeating a long setup. The retained replay contains no miss or failed jump, so this is a source-and-cue estimate, replacing the first-pass unknown without claiming observed recovery.

evidence.claim: The visible start prompt says to wait at the side if the lift is missed.
A continuous floor lies below the periodic lift, providing a safe place to reset position.
The lift follows a repeating motion path.

solution_clarity.rationale: The text says the lift takes two cells and gives a left-side jump plus a safe wait instruction; the RESTORE label and earlier pad lesson help. Still, the exact requirement that both players occupy the attached pad together is not stated outright and requires connecting the cell count to the two characters. The first-pass clarity burden 2 is retained.

evidence.claim: Visible onboarding says the lift takes two cells to restart.
The frame shows the lift, two heroes, RESTORE area, and jump-from-left/wait-at-side cue.
Source clarifies that the two-weight condition applies to occupancy of the attached RESTORE pad.

control_friction.rationale: The replay is a scripted input schedule and provides no evidence about two humans' reliability or interference while sharing the keyboard.

evidence.claim: The native replay report says its feasibility evidence does not establish input reliability.

confidence_reason: Current source and a detailed current-source replay establish the door handoff, two-hero activation threshold, lift ride, and both-exit completion. No human discovery, failed ride, actual recovery, or two-human control reliability was observed.

confirmed: The visible two-cell lift instruction corresponds to a two-weight activation condition on RESTORE.
The prior level_02 pad and bubble concepts are relevant: Isp uses a hold pad again, and Gem's bubble remains a role-specific interference effect.
The two-exit objective remains the mandatory goal; collectibles remain separate.
missed_mechanics: Both heroes must occupy the lift-attached RESTORE pad at once; one hero alone produces weight 1 and leaves the pad inactive.
The latched RESTORE pad powers a requires-power lift and reopens the DNA wall, after which the lift carries both riders to the exit balcony.
The visible recovery cue says a missed lift can be retried by waiting at the side; the route does not depend on an unrecoverable single window.
changed_judgments: Reasoning rose from 2 to 3 because the two-cell condition is a simultaneous two-hero activation that powers the moving lift and restores the wall, after an earlier door-opening dependency.
Cooperation changed from unknown to 4 because source and trace establish both a door handoff and a coordinated simultaneous two-hero pad activation.
Execution changed from unknown to 3 because the sampled route includes multiple jumps, shared pad placement, a moving-lift ride, and a jump to the balcony.
Timing changed from unknown to 2 because boarding follows a readable repeating lift cycle and the screen gives a safe wait-at-side recovery cue.

Hazards changed from unknown to 0 because the route is supported by a continuous floor, has no authored hazards, and completed without death; temporary bubble effects are interference, not physical hazard exposure here.
Novelty rose from 2 to 3 because source clarified a new simultaneous weight-to-power moving-lift model, beyond the earlier room's sequential hold-and-rescue door pads.
Recovery cost changed from unknown to 1 because a missed ride can likely be retried from the side on a repeating lift; this recovery was cued but not exercised.
Solution clarity stayed at burden 2: the words 'two cells' and the jump/wait cues help, but the joint-pad occupancy requirement remains an inference for players.
unresolved: Whether first-time players connect 'two cells' to both heroes sharing the RESTORE pad without using a hint.
How reliably two humans synchronize their jumps and movement onto the attached pad.
How actual players recover after a missed boarding attempt or a premature release of DNA_OPEN.

single_operator_note: A single operator would need to manage both key clusters while coordinating a two-hero jump onto the same moving lift pad, then ride and jump to the balcony. The shared-keyboard baseline assumes two humans; one-operator interference was not measured.
